attacks.claim: The chosen vendor tier cannot support the architecture. chain_poller needs 160 req/min of real-time chain snapshots, but Starter allows 5 req/min and serves 15-minute-delayed option quotes. Intraday triggers and limit pricing would run on stale data, defeating the plan's premise.
attacks.evidence: "We stay on Starter." vs. "Starter | $79 | 5 req/min | 15-min delayed" and "40 underlyings => 160 requests/min during RTH"

attacks.claim: The $250/month cap is breached by any tier that can do the job. Growth is $199 + $60 VPS = $259 and still only 100 req/min (below the 160 needed). Pro is $499. The '$139, comfortably inside the cap' figure holds only for a tier that cannot run the engine.
attacks.evidence: "Monthly run cost: Optiq Starter $79 + existing VPS $60 = $139, comfortably inside the $250 cap."

attacks.claim: Migration 0042 irreversibly drops prod roll_history, including all entries older than 90 days that are not backfilled, in one in-place transaction. No backup, snapshot, rehearsal, or down-migration is stated. The 'not needed' claim covers only roll_engine, and no retention or tax/audit need is addressed.
attacks.evidence: "In the same transaction, ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history." and "older entries are not needed by roll_engine."; ABSENT: backup, rollback, or retention/archive step

attacks.claim: The roll_eod.py fallback is not real after the migration. The column it likely reads is dropped in week 1, and the plan does not confirm that it does not read roll_history. Rollback to the EOD path may be unavailable exactly when needed.
attacks.evidence: "roll_eod.py stays deployed behind ROLLER_V2=false as the fallback path through week 4." alongside "ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history."

attacks.claim: Safety controls do not cover live orders or stale data. The heartbeat guard and ROLLER_KILL only stop new intents, so working combo orders (up to 3 re-prices) are not cancelled or reconciled. There is no snapshot staleness or sanity check, and no 429/backoff handling for chain_poller. A failed roll after 3 re-prices leaves the short call open with no fallback or alert. An env-var kill switch has no stated way to be flipped at runtime.
attacks.evidence: "roll_engine stops emitting intents when the last successful broker heartbeat is > 60 s old."; "re-priced every 20 s up to 3 times, then cancelled"; "ROLLER_KILL env switch read on every loop"; ABSENT: order cancellation on kill/heartbeat loss, snapshot max-age check

attacks.claim: The 8-orders-per-account-per-day cap across 40 underlyings can leave short calls unrolled on broad volatile days, the exact days the design targets. There is no prioritization rule, and it is unclear whether re-prices count against the caps. The roll-target rule is also undefined for a credit under $0.05 or a debit.
attacks.evidence: "max 1 roll per contract per day and max 8 roll orders per account per day"; "next strike up if the credit is >= $0.05"

attacks.claim: There is no monitoring, alerting, or operator visibility. Poller failures, rate-limit errors, failed combos, and kill-switch state go unobserved during live sessions.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: metrics, alerts, dashboards, or on-call ownership in §3, §6, §7

attacks.claim: The +3.8% net APR claim has no backtest or cost model. It rests on hindsight desk notes and an unsourced appeal to peer funds. Paper mode compares intents only, with no fills, and runs on the delayed tier, so it cannot validate the thesis. The 30-day live criterion cannot be completed within the 4-week schedule that moves to all 40 names, and there are no go/no-go gates between 5 and 40 underlyings.
attacks.evidence: "Expected impact: +3.8% net APR vs. EOD rolling"; "Desk notes ... 'would have been better'"; "Week 4: ROLLER_V2=true on 5 underlyings, then all 40."

attacks.claim: The plan does not address vendor data-license terms for automated trading, or the tax/wash-sale and day-trading implications of materially increased intraday roll frequency.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: review of Optiq Data terms, tax, wash-sale, or pattern-day-trading analysis

attacks.claim: Snapshot persistence and retention are unspecified for roughly 230k fetches per day. The design also relies on a single data vendor with no secondary feed. The trigger semantics are labelled 'unchanged' although a new 4% gap trigger and next-strike rule are added, and the gap reference point is undefined.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: snapshot retention policy; "Roll triggers (unchanged semantics, new timing)"; "Underlying gaps > 4% through strike"
